## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

**2026-06-16 — OpenAI: GPT-5-codex available in Responses API**  
Primary source: [OpenAI Help Center — Model Release Notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes?pscd=get.youai.ai&ps_partner_key=ZGF2aWRsZXZpbm92NjA3NA&ps_xid=Z9sp46w9U8Fl1f&gsxid=Z9sp46w9U8Fl1f&gspk=ZGF2aWRsZXZpbm92NjA3NA)  
OpenAI’s release notes say GPT-5-codex is now available through the Responses API, extending access beyond Codex-specific surfaces.  
**Why it matters:** This moves OpenAI’s coding-specialized model into a more general API workflow, making it easier to integrate into developer tools, CI agents, and custom coding automation.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

**2026-06-16 — Z.ai releases GLM-5.2**  
Primary source: [Z.ai docs — GLM-5.2](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.2)  
Z.ai added GLM-5.2, described as a flagship text model for long-horizon coding and agent tasks, with 1M-token context, 128K max output, thinking modes, function calling, structured output, context caching, and MCP support. The provided research notes say the Hugging Face card lists it under an MIT license.  
**Why it matters:** A permissively licensed, long-context agent/coding model increases pressure on closed coding-model offerings and gives enterprises another candidate for self-hosted agent workflows.

## 3. Major Financial AI Company News

**2026-06-15 — Sarvam raises $234M Series B at $1.5B valuation**  
Primary source: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/15/sarvam-becomes-indias-newest-ai-unicorn-with-234-million-funding-round-led-by-hcltech/)  
India-based Sarvam raised $234M led by HCLTech, with participation from Bessemer and existing investors.  
**Why it matters:** The round strengthens India’s sovereign-AI stack and gives Sarvam more capital to compete in regional-language models and government/enterprise AI infrastructure.

**2026-06-15 — Respond.io raises $62.5M for AI customer messaging**  
Primary source: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/15/malaysias-respond-io-raises-62-5m-eyes-acquisitions-in-north-america-and-europe/)  
Malaysia-based Respond.io raised a $62.5M Series B led by Camber Partners. Its product uses AI agents across messaging, voice, and web chat channels.  
**Why it matters:** Funding is moving into operational AI agents for customer engagement, especially in markets where WhatsApp, Line, WeChat, and social commerce are primary customer channels.

## 4. Major AI Data Center News

**2026-06-15 — Google commits $1.5B to Alabama data center expansion**  
Primary source: [Google Blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/infrastructure-and-cloud/global-network/alabama-investment-june-2026/)  
Google announced $1.5B in 2026-2027 investments to expand its Jackson County, Alabama data center campus.  
**Why it matters:** Hyperscaler AI capacity buildout remains capital-intensive and geographically distributed; Alabama continues to be part of Google’s U.S. infrastructure footprint.

**2026-06-16 — Data center deployment increasingly tied to grid flexibility**  
Primary source: [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/06/16/1138591/data-center-online-quickly-electric-grid-flex/)  
MIT Technology Review examined how flexible power demand can help data centers come online faster despite grid constraints.  
**Why it matters:** AI infrastructure timelines are increasingly governed by power availability, not only chips or construction. Demand flexibility is becoming a strategic deployment lever.

## 5. Regulation & Policy

**2026-06-16 — DOJ backs xAI in lawsuit over unpermitted gas turbines**  
Primary source: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/16/doj-claims-xais-unpermitted-gas-turbines-are-a-matter-of-national-economic-and-energy-security/)  
The Justice Department argued that shutting down xAI gas turbines near Memphis-area AI data centers would harm national, economic, and energy security.  
**Why it matters:** The federal position ties AI data center power supply directly to national-security framing, potentially raising the stakes for local environmental enforcement disputes.
